title: The Multimodal Future of Education: Stefania Druga
talk_summary: This is an education-research talk about AI literacy for children and families, describing the open-source 'Cognimates' Scratch extension and a family co-pilot study, plus live Gemini multimodal demos that ask Socratic questions about drawings.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of answering, the model responds to a student's work with a guiding question so the learner keeps iterating; the demo explicitly refuses to give the final answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it doesn't give me the answer it just give me a question so I can keep trying right and learning

takeaways.what_they_do: They built a benchmark of the most common K-12 math misconceptions to measure whether top models can detect the misconception behind a student's utterance, not just whether the final answer is right.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we created the first Benchmark for math misconceptions to show what are the most common math problems

takeaways.what_they_do: Longitudinal study asks the same questions before and after an intervention to isolate the effect of the learning activity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we asked questions of what kids think about AI before then we allow them to engage in AI learning activities and then we ask the same questions at the end

takeaways.what_they_do: A minimal open-source template wraps a multimodal API with custom instructions so anyone can tinker quickly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I made the code open source and template so you can play with it too is less than 100 lines
